title: Incident
description: A driving-behaviour or collision event involving a THIRD-PARTY vehicle observed from the bus. Structurally different from an Observation: an Observation is a per-frame detection of a static thing, an Incident is a conclusion drawn from a TRACKED TRAJECTORY over a time window. Incidents pre-empt the uplink queue entirely and are transmitted immediately. MQTT topic: argus/v1/{fleet}/{device_id}/incident (QoS 2)

incident_type.description: hit_and_run is collision + the offending track departing the scene above a speed threshold. The distinction is made from trajectory, not from intent.

triggers.description: The kinematic evidence that fired the classifier. Recorded so a human reviewer can audit WHY the system concluded an incident, rather than being asked to trust a score.

ttc_s.description: Minimum time-to-collision observed against the subject track, in seconds.

lateral_accel_ms2.description: Peak lateral acceleration of the subject track.

lane_changes.description: Lane crossings by the subject track within the window.

ego_impact_g.description: Peak IMU magnitude on the bus. The primary collision trigger; a camera can miss an impact the chassis cannot.

track_discontinuity.description: Subject trajectory broke in a way consistent with a collision rather than occlusion.

departure_speed_kmh.description: Subject speed leaving the scene. Separates hit_and_run from collision.

vru_proximity_m.description: Closest approach to a tracked pedestrian or cyclist.

subject_vehicle.description: The offending vehicle, as reconstructed from its track.

plate.description: ANPR result. The plate string is assembled by PER-CHARACTER MAJORITY VOTE across every frame of the track, not read from a single best frame. A single 640p read from a moving bus is unreliable; voting across 20+ frames is not, and it produces a genuine confidence figure rather than a softmax score.

confidence.description: Product of per-character vote margins. This is the confidence score the problem statement asks for.

per_character_confidence.description: Exposed so an operator can see WHICH character is uncertain. A plate reading 0.94 overall but 0.41 on one digit is actionable in a way a single scalar is not.

state_code_valid.description: Whether the leading two letters are a real RTO state code. A cheap, strong sanity filter on OCR output.

evidence.description: The one case where video, not a crop, leaves the bus. A pre-roll buffer means the clip starts BEFORE the trigger.

duration_s.description: Typically 30 s: 10 s pre-roll plus 20 s post-trigger.

encrypted.description: Incident clips are encrypted at rest. Access is logged against an operator identity.
